findings.title: traceID no longer included in 'Plugin Request Completed' log line
findings.body: The previous implementation of logRequest explicitly extracted the trace ID via `tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false)` and appended it as a `traceID` log field. This PR removes that logic entirely (the `tracing` import was dropped from this file) and the new `ContextualLoggerMiddleware.instrumentContext` that replaces the removed context-enrichment code only adds `endpoint`, `pluginId`, `dsName`, `dsUID` and `uname` - it does not add `traceID`. Unless the underlying infra logger automatically injects trace IDs from the context (not evidenced anywhere in this diff), this change silently drops trace correlation information from the 'Plugin Request Completed' log entries, which is a regression for anyone correlating logs with traces.

findings.title: New ContextualLoggerMiddleware has no unit tests
findings.body: This PR introduces a brand-new middleware, `ContextualLoggerMiddleware`, which is responsible for enriching the context with plugin/request attributes used by downstream logging (notably `LoggerMiddleware`, which now relies on `FromContext(ctx)` to pick up these attributes). No test file (e.g. contextual_logger_middleware_test.go) was added to verify that QueryData/CallResource/CheckHealth/CollectMetrics correctly attach the expected contextual attributes, or that SubscribeStream/PublishStream/RunStream intentionally do not. Given that this logic was previously covered indirectly inside the (deleted) instrumentation middleware tests, extracting it into its own middleware without dedicated tests leaves this behavior unverified.

findings.title: Missing documentation of required middleware ordering
findings.body: The previous `InstrumentationMiddleware` had an explicit comment stating it must be placed at the top of the middleware stack because it both records metrics and enriches the context with a contextual logger. After this refactor, `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` must still be placed before `LoggerMiddleware` (and any other middleware that wants the enriched contextual logger) in the stack for the logging to pick up the attributes via `FromContext`. This ordering constraint is no longer documented anywhere (neither on `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` nor on `LoggerMiddleware`), making it easy for a future change to reorder middlewares (e.g. in pluginsintegration.go) and silently lose the contextual log attributes without any test or compiler error to catch the regression.

findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext discards state, making contextual logging unverifiable in tests
findings.body: `TestLogger.FromContext` always returns a brand-new `TestLogger` instance via `NewTestLogger()`, rather than returning the receiver `f` (or otherwise preserving the recorded `InfoLogs`/`WarnLogs`/etc. fields). Since `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest` now calls `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)` instead of logging directly on `m.logger`, any test that uses `TestLogger` to assert on the 'Plugin Request Completed' log output (e.g. checking `InfoLogs.Calls`/`Message`) will observe no change on the original logger instance, because the actual `Info` call lands on a disposable, unreferenced `TestLogger` returned by `FromContext`. This effectively makes `TestLogger` unusable for verifying any code path that logs via `FromContext`, which is now the primary logging path for plugin client middlewares.

findings.title: Test function name not updated after Instrumentation→Metrics rename
findings.body: The file was renamed from instrumentation_middleware_test.go to metrics_middleware_test.go and the helper `newInstrumentationMiddleware` call site was updated to `newMetricsMiddleware`, but the test function itself is still named `TestInstrumentationMiddleware`. This is inconsistent with the stated goal of the PR ('Renamed instrumentation middleware to metrics middleware') and leaves stale naming that should have been updated to `TestMetricsMiddleware` for consistency with the rest of the rename.
